# Slider

Header: `winui/ui/input/Slider.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/input/Slider.hpp`.

A thumb dragged along a track to pick a value in [[min()](#min), [max()](#max)].

A click on the track jumps the thumb there and starts a drag; the drag snaps to [step_frequency()](#step_frequency) (or the ticks, see [set_snaps_to()](#set_snaps_to)). The arrow keys move by [step()](#step), Home and End jump to the ends, and [on_value_changed()](#on_value_changed) fires live on every change. An optional header sits above the track. The declarative form is [ui::Slider](#uislider).

Example: 
```cpp
auto  panel  = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* label  = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("50"));
auto* volume = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::SliderControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal,
                                                          0.0f, 100.0f, 50.0f));
volume->set_header("Volume");
volume->set_step(5.0f);
volume->set_tick_frequency(10.0f);
volume->set_tick_placement(ui::SliderTickPlacement::BottomRight);
volume->on_value_changed([label](double v) { label->set_text(std::format("{:.0f}", v)); });
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

## `ui::Slider`

A draggable thumb over a continuous range. Builds a [ui::SliderControl](#uislidercontrol).

[`orientation`](#uislider-orientation), the range and the initial value go to the control's constructor, so the value is clamped against the right range from the start and seeding it raises nothing.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<double> volume{40.0};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .spacing  = 8,
    .content  = {
        ui::Slider{.header           = "Volume",
                   .value            = volume,
                   .max              = 100.0,
                   .step             = 5.0,
                   .tick_frequency   = 10.0,
                   .tick_placement   = ui::SliderTickPlacement::BottomRight,
                   .width            = 240.0f},
        ui::Text{.text = ui::bind(volume, [](double v) { return std::format("{:.0f}%", v); })},
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Slider{
    .header, .value, .min, .max, .step, .tick_frequency, .tick_placement, .step_frequency,
    .snaps_to, .orientation, .direction_reversed, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width,
    .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible,
    .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility, .on_value_changed, .on_pointer_entered,
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uislider-header"></span>`header` | `ui::Binding<std::string>` |  | The label above the control. Empty draws none. |
| <span id="uislider-value"></span>`value` | `ui::TwoWayField<double>` | `{0.0}` | Value, clamped to [[`min`](#uislider-min), [`max`](#uislider-max)]. `ui::bind(prop)` is two-way: dragging writes the property. |
| <span id="uislider-min"></span>`min` | `ui::Binding<double>` | `{0.0}` | Minimum, the value at the start of the track. A bound range that moves past the value clamps it, and a two-way [`value`](#uislider-value) follows. |
| <span id="uislider-max"></span>`max` | `ui::Binding<double>` | `{100.0}` | Maximum, the value at the end of the track. Below [`min`](#uislider-min), it is taken as [`min`](#uislider-min). |
| <span id="uislider-step"></span>`step` | `ui::Binding<double>` | `{1.0}` | What an arrow key adds or takes away; 0 turns arrow stepping off. |
| <span id="uislider-tick_frequency"></span>`tick_frequency` | `ui::Binding<double>` | `{0.0}` | See [ui::SliderControl::set_tick_frequency](#set_tick_frequency): 0 draws no ticks, except under the classic look. |
| <span id="uislider-tick_placement"></span>`tick_placement` | `ui::Binding<ui::SliderTickPlacement>` | `{ui::SliderTickPlacement::Inline}` | Where the ticks go relative to the track; [Inline](../tree/inline.md) (across it) by default. |
| <span id="uislider-step_frequency"></span>`step_frequency` | `ui::Binding<double>` | `{1.0}` | What a drag snaps to: 1 by default, 0 for a continuous drag. [`step`](#uislider-step) stays the arrow-key increment. |
| <span id="uislider-snaps_to"></span>`snaps_to` | `ui::Binding<ui::SliderSnapsTo>` | `{ui::SliderSnapsTo::StepValues}` | A drag lands on [`step_frequency`](#uislider-step_frequency) multiples, or on ticks (which the arrow keys then move by too). |
| <span id="uislider-orientation"></span>`orientation` | `ui::Orientation` | `ui::Orientation::Horizontal` | Horizontal or Vertical; fixed at build time (the control has no setter for it). |
| <span id="uislider-direction_reversed"></span>`direction_reversed` | `ui::Binding<bool>` | `{false}` | Min at the right (horizontal) or the top (vertical). |
| <span id="uislider-on_value_changed"></span>`on_value_changed` | `ui::Callback<void(double)>` |  | The new value, live on every change during a drag, click or key press. A bound value doesn't run it. |
| <span id="uislider-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uislider-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uislider-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uislider-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uislider-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uislider-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uislider-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::Slider>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

## `ui::SliderControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::RangeValueProvider`.

A thumb dragged along a track to pick a value in [[min()](#min), [max()](#max)].

A click on the track jumps the thumb there and starts a drag; the drag snaps to [step_frequency()](#step_frequency) (or the ticks, see [set_snaps_to()](#set_snaps_to)). The arrow keys move by [step()](#step), Home and End jump to the ends, and [on_value_changed()](#on_value_changed) fires live on every change. An optional header sits above the track. The declarative form is [ui::Slider](#uislider).

Example: 
```cpp
auto  panel  = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* label  = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("50"));
auto* volume = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::SliderControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal,
                                                          0.0f, 100.0f, 50.0f));
volume->set_header("Volume");
volume->set_step(5.0f);
volume->set_tick_frequency(10.0f);
volume->set_tick_placement(ui::SliderTickPlacement::BottomRight);
volume->on_value_changed([label](double v) { label->set_text(std::format("{:.0f}", v)); });
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

### SliderControl

```cpp
SliderControl(Orientation orientation = Orientation::Horizontal, double min = 0.0, double max = 100.0, double value = 0.0)
```

A slider over [min, max] starting at [`value`](#value) (clamped into the range). Raises nothing.

```cpp
Orientation orientation() const
```

The orientation given at construction; there is no setter.

```cpp

```

The header text; empty when none is shown.

### set_header

```cpp
void set_header(std::string header)
```

The label above the slider. Empty draws none.

### min

```cpp
double min() const
```

The value at the start of the track.

### max

```cpp
double max() const
```

The value at the end of the track; never below [min()](#min).

### set_range

```cpp
void set_range(double min, double max)
```

Sets the range and clamps the current value into it, firing on_value_changed if that moves it. A [`max`](#max) below [`min`](#min) is taken as [`min`](#min).

### value

```cpp
double value() const
```

Value, always within [[min()](#min), [max()](#max)].

### set_value

```cpp
void set_value(double value)
```

Clamps to [min, max]. Fires on_value_changed only if the clamped value differs from the current one.

### step

```cpp
double step() const
```

The arrow-key increment, 1 by default. Also UI Automation's small change.

### set_step

```cpp
void set_step(double step)
```

The amount each arrow-key press moves the value by. Zero disables keyboard stepping (Home/End still jump to min/max). Negative is 0.

### tick_frequency

```cpp
double tick_frequency() const
```

The tick interval in value units; 0 (the default) means none is set.

### set_tick_frequency

```cpp
void set_tick_frequency(double frequency)
```

How often a tick mark is drawn along the track, in value units. Ticks sit at whole multiples of it counted from [min()](#min), one at [min()](#min) and one per full interval after, so a range the frequency does not divide gets no tick at [max()](#max). Ticks closer than 20 DIPs are thinned to every n-th one.

At zero there are no ticks, though some themes still mark the two ends of the range. Negative is 0. Redraws only.

### tick_placement

```cpp
SliderTickPlacement tick_placement() const
```

Where the ticks go relative to the track; [Inline](../tree/inline.md) by default.

### set_tick_placement

```cpp
void set_tick_placement(SliderTickPlacement placement)
```

Redraws only.

### step_frequency

```cpp
double step_frequency() const
```

The drag snapping interval, 1 by default.

### set_step_frequency

```cpp
void set_step_frequency(double frequency)
```

The interval a pointer click or drag snaps to under SliderSnapsTo::StepValues. It is 1 by default, so a drag lands on whole values. Give a range narrower than a few units a finer step. Zero makes the drag continuous. Snapping lands on whole multiples of the interval counted from 0, not from [min()](#min), clamped into the range. Keyboard stepping uses [step()](#step) and is unaffected. [set_value()](#set_value) never snaps.

### snaps_to

```cpp
SliderSnapsTo snaps_to() const
```

What a drag snaps to; StepValues by default.

### set_snaps_to

```cpp
void set_snaps_to(SliderSnapsTo snaps_to)
```

SliderSnapsTo::Ticks snaps a drag to [tick_frequency()](#tick_frequency) instead and makes the arrow keys move by it, ignoring [step()](#step). With no tick frequency set it behaves as StepValues.

### direction_reversed

```cpp
bool direction_reversed() const
```

Reverses the direction: min at the right of a horizontal slider and at the top of a vertical one, with the value fill, the ticks, a click, a drag and the arrow keys all following (Left and Down then increase, Right and Up decrease). False by default.

### set_direction_reversed

```cpp
void set_direction_reversed(bool reversed)
```

Redraws; the value itself does not change.

### set_track_gradient

```cpp
void set_track_gradient(std::optional<LinearGradientBrush> gradient, bool checkerboard = false)
```

Draws the whole track with `gradient`, in place of the neutral track and the accent fill up to the thumb. `checkerboard` draws a 50% checkerboard (Pattern::Checkerboard50) behind the gradient first, so a channel whose stops carry partial alpha looks translucent. std::nullopt restores the default track. The retro (95/98/2000) bevel track ignores the gradient.

### on_value_changed

```cpp
void on_value_changed(Callback<void(double)> handler)
```

Fired whenever [`value`](#value) changes, from a drag, a click-to-jump, or a keyboard step alike. A drag fires on every change, not only on release.


The header, when set, is stacked above the track ([ControlHeader](../tree/control-header.md)). The track asks for 200 DIPs along its axis (less if less is offered) and at least 32 across it.

```cpp

```

Press on the track jumps the value there and starts a drag; moves while dragging update the value (snapped per [snaps_to()](#snaps_to)); release ends the drag.

Draws the header, the track (or [set_track_gradient()](#set_track_gradient)'s gradient), the value fill, the ticks and the thumb, or the classic track and thumb under a retro theme.

### enabled_changed

```cpp

```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.


Arrow keys step by [step()](#step) (or the tick frequency under SliderSnapsTo::Ticks), Home/End jump to [min()](#min)/max().


Around the thumb, the track's row or the whole control, as the theme places it. None where focus shows on the thumb's face.

### focus_ring_corner_radius

The ring's corner radius: the theme's control radius by default.

## Enumerations

### SliderTickPlacement

```cpp
enum class SliderTickPlacement
```

Where tick marks are drawn relative to the track. No placement draws ticks until tick_frequency() is above zero, except under the classic look. The classic look only tells None (no ticks) from the rest, which all draw its one row of ticks on the far side (see set_tick_frequency()).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | no ticks |
| `TopLeft` | above a horizontal track, left of a vertical one |
| `BottomRight` | below a horizontal track, right of a vertical one |
| `Outside` | both of the above |
| `Inline` | notches cut across the track itself (the default) |

### SliderSnapsTo

```cpp
enum class SliderSnapsTo
```

What a pointer drag lands on.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `StepValues` | multiples of step_frequency() |
| `Ticks` | multiples of tick_frequency(); the arrow keys move by it too |
